paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God keeps His work going even when people don't agree and even when the road gets blocked. Paul and Barnabas had a disagreement so sharp that they parted company (Acts 15:39). I think that one hurt. But Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus, Paul chose Silas, and the writer shows two teams heading out instead of one team stuck in the argument.

Then the doors start shutting. The Holy Spirit prevented them from speaking the word in Asia, and the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them to enter Bithynia (Acts 16:6-7). Friend, I know what a shut door feels like, and I'd have stood there pushing on it all day. But a closed door isn't always a punishment. Sometimes it's the Lord steering you toward a different door, and it's still the work He wants done.

So what do you do with this, baker? Keep strengthening and keep delivering what you've been given, because the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew daily in numbers while the team kept moving (Acts 16:5). Then when the call comes, do what they did: they concluded that God had called them, and they got ready to go (Acts 16:10). Keep your oven warm, listen close, and when He opens the door, GO.
